hook.convey: path from start = 0 to finish = 1; walker stops exactly halfway → stands on a real spot → whole numbers 0, 1 have no name for it → fractions = numbers that live between 0 and 1
hook.slotUse: the one-whole length from start (0) to finish (1) that gets cut into equal gaps; the stopping point is a spot on that length, never a count of things

explain.convey: 0 and 1 at the ends; one cut exactly in the middle → 2 equal gaps; the middle mark = 1/2 → 1/2 is a number with its own place, between 0 and 1, not at 2
explain.point: the single middle mark labelled 1/2, halfway between 0 and 1

explain.convey: same 0 to 1, now 3 marks inside → 4 equal gaps (gaps = marks inside + 1); bottom number = number of equal gaps in 0 to 1; first mark from 0 = end of 1 gap = 1/4; name comes from gaps, not marks
explain.point: the 4 equal gaps between 0 and 1 and the first mark after 0 labelled 1/4

explain.convey: each quarter halved → 8 equal gaps → each gap smaller; 1/8 = first mark, right next to 0; 1/2 still at the middle (4 of 8 gaps); bigger bottom number → smaller gap → unit fraction sits closer to 0
explain.point: the 1/8 mark hugging 0 against the 1/2 mark in the middle

workedExample.problem: Mark 1/4 on a number line from 0 to 1.
workedExample.find: the mark on the line that is 1/4

steps.do: draw the line; write 0 at the left end, 1 at the right end
bottom number 4 → split 0 to 1 into 4 equal gaps
steps.result: 4 equal gaps, made by 3 marks in between

steps.do: value of one gap = 1 whole ÷ 4 equal gaps
check against the middle: 1/2 = 2 of the 4 gaps; 1 gap < 2 gaps
steps.result: 1/4 is before the middle, between 0 and 1/2

workedExample.answer: 1/4 is the first of the 3 marks after 0, at the end of the first of 4 equal gaps
workedExample.why: bottom number = equal gaps in one whole → each gap = 1/4; top number = gaps moved from 0 → 1 gap → first mark; marks are only the cuts, gaps are the parts

checks.prompt: A line from 0 to 1 has 2 equally spaced marks in between. What fraction is the first mark after 0?
On a line from 0 to 1, which is closer to 0: 1/3 or 1/10?
On a number line from 0 to 3, between which two whole numbers does 1/2 lie?

ladder.why: den 2: one cut, gaps obvious → fraction as a place on the road; same den as e1
den 4 (halves halved, as in e2 and the worked example) → 2nd mark = 2/4 → same spot as 1/2; gap-value thinking, not mark counting
den 6 given as gaps → apply bottom = gaps to a new den outside the halving family 2 → 4 → 8
den 5 given only as marks (4 inside) → must convert marks to gaps; error-spot on the count-marks trap
den 6 again but given as 5 inside marks → contrasts with rl-o1 (same den, gaps given) → explain why the label is wrong

remediation.move: ribbon at a tailor's shop, 0 to 1 m; marks = scissor cuts, gaps = ribbon pieces; cuts inside + 1 = pieces; fraction names a piece of length, so bottom number = pieces the metre falls into; 3 cuts → 4 pieces → first cut at 1/4 m
remediation.then: ribbon 0 to 1 m with 6 equally spaced cuts inside → length from 0 to the first cut, as a fraction of a metre

remediation.move: two equal 0-to-1 strips laid on one line: one cut into 2, one into 5; first piece of each laid from 0; 1/5 stops at 2 of 10 tenths, 1/2 at 5 of 10 → more pieces in the same whole → each piece shorter → 1/5 stops sooner
remediation.then: two equal 0-to-1 strips: one cut into 3 equal pieces, one into 6 → which strip's first piece, laid from 0, stops sooner

remediation.move: road from home (0) to chai stall (1 km), milestones every 1/4 km; toy walks from home and stops halfway, at the 2nd milestone → toy stands on one spot of the road → that spot has a number, 1/2 km = 2/4 km → numbers exist between 0 and 1
remediation.then: road from home (0) to chai stall (1 km) cut into 8 equal stretches; toy stops at the end of the first stretch → the number it stands on

skills.bridgeToNext: 1 gap from 0 = 1/bottom → keep moving more gaps from 0 → 2 gaps, 3 gaps → top number = gaps moved from 0

hook.convey: same 0-to-1 path cut into equal stretches; stop is not at the first mark but several stretches on → name needs two facts: how many equal stretches make the whole, how many have been covered
hook.slotUse: the 0-to-1 length cut into equal stretches, and a stopping point several stretches from 0

explain.convey: thirds: bottom 3 → 0 to 1 in 3 equal gaps; top 2 → 2 hops of 1/3 from 0; landing mark = 2/3 → one point, one number, not 2 and 3 separately
explain.point: the two hops from 0 ending at the mark labelled 2/3

explain.convey: still thirds: 3 hops of 1/3 → every gap used → land exactly on 1 → 3/3 = 1; top < bottom → stop before 1; top = bottom → reach 1
explain.point: the third hop landing on 1, labelled 3/3 = 1

explain.convey: each third cut in 2 → 6 equal gaps; middle = half the gaps = 3/6 = 1/2; fewer than half the gaps (2/6) → before the middle; more than half (5/6) → after the middle
explain.point: the middle mark 3/6 = 1/2, with 2/6 to its left and 5/6 to its right

workedExample.problem: Mark 2/5 on a number line from 0 to 1.
workedExample.find: the mark on the line that is 2/5

steps.do: draw the line; 0 at the left end, 1 at the right end
bottom number 5 → split 0 to 1 into 5 equal gaps
steps.result: 5 equal gaps, made by 4 marks in between

steps.do: value of one gap = 1 whole ÷ 5 equal gaps
check against the middle: half of 5 gaps = 2 and a half gaps; 2 gaps < 2 and a half gaps

workedExample.answer: 2/5 is the 2nd mark after 0 when 0 to 1 is split into 5 equal gaps
workedExample.why: bottom number = equal gaps in the whole → each gap 1/5; top number = gaps moved from 0 → 2 gaps → 2nd mark; fewer than half the gaps → before 1/2

checks.prompt: A line from 0 to 1 has 5 equally spaced marks in between. What fraction is the 4th mark after 0?
On a line from 0 to 1, which is closer to 1: 3/4 or 3/8?
On a number line from 0 to 5, between which two whole numbers does 3/4 lie?
checks.wrongIfMis: at 3 and 4 (reads 3/4 as the two numbers 3 and 4)

ladder.why: den 4: quarters already known from s1 and the c4 roti → carry a shaded 3 of 4 onto the line; top = gaps moved
den 5: same den as the worked example → locate 3/5 by gaps moved from 0, now one step further than 2/5
den 5 reversed: given the mark, name the fraction → 4/5 km; read the line instead of marking it
den 10: each fifth split in 2 → many small gaps, unit given as 1/10 km → 7 steps = 7/10
den 8 against den 4 → two different cuts, same stopping point (6/8 = 3/4); closes the loop back to quarters

remediation.move: hop arrows instead of marks: each hop = one equal gap = 1/6; hops start at 0, the start is not a hop; fraction = hops made over hops that fill 0 to 1; 4 hops of 1/6 → 4/6
remediation.then: ribbon from 0 to 1 m with 5 equally spaced cuts inside; tailor measures from 0 to the 2nd cut → fraction of a metre

remediation.move: same number of hops, different hop size: 3 hops of 1/10 vs 3 hops of 1/5 on one 0-to-1 line; tenth-hops are half as long as fifth-hops → 3/10 stops at 3 tenths, 3/5 at 6 tenths → bigger bottom number = shorter hops = stop nearer 0
remediation.then: from 0 on a 0-to-1 line: 2 hops of 1/4 or 2 hops of 1/8 → which stops sooner

remediation.move: km stones on a highway from 0 to 1 km, a stone every 1/4 km; toy walks 3 stretches and stops → stands on one single stone → that stone's number is 3/4 km, one point between 0 and 1, not two numbers
remediation.then: highway from 0 to 1 km with a stone every 1/5 km; toy stops at the 2nd stone after 0 → the one number it stands on

skills.bridgeToNext: top < bottom → stop before 1; top = bottom → land on 1 (3/3); top > bottom → gaps run out at 1 → keep hopping past 1 on a longer line

hook.convey: runner finishes one full lap and keeps going → stopping point past 1 → needs a fraction name bigger than 1 → line must go beyond 1
hook.slotUse: the unit that repeats (one lap, one km, one station-to-station stretch) and a stopping point beyond the first unit

explain.convey: line does not stop at 1 → carries on to 2; second whole cut the same way → 4 equal gaps per whole, all the same size; 4 gaps from 0 = 4/4 = 1; gap count from 0 keeps growing past 4
explain.point: the mark at 1 labelled 4/4 = 1, with the same-size quarter gaps continuing on to 2

explain.convey: 6 hops of 1/4 from 0: first 4 hops fill one whole → reach 1; 2 more hops → past 1 → 6/4 = 1 and 2/4; top > bottom → beyond 1
explain.point: the six hops from 0, crossing 1 and landing on the mark labelled 6/4

explain.convey: thirds on a line to 3: every 3 gaps = one whole → 3/3 = 1; group gaps in threes to find which whole a fraction has passed; top above 3 → past 1
explain.point: the first group of 3 third-gaps ending at 1, labelled 3/3 = 1, and the line continuing in thirds to 3

workedExample.problem: Mark 7/4 on a number line from 0 to 2.
workedExample.find: the mark on the line that is 7/4

steps.result: line from 0 to 2 with 1 in the middle

steps.do: bottom number 4 → split each whole (0 to 1, 1 to 2) into 4 equal gaps
top 7 > bottom 4 → fraction is more than 1
4 gaps from 0 fill the first whole

steps.result: 7/4 is between 1 and 2, one gap before 2; 7/4 = 1 and 3/4

workedExample.answer: 7/4 is the 3rd mark after 1 (1 and 3/4), one quarter-gap before 2
workedExample.why: bottom number = equal gaps in each whole, so every whole holds 4 quarters; 4 quarters fill 1 → 3 quarters left over → 3 gaps past 1; a fraction is a length from 0 and lengths can be longer than one whole

checks.prompt: On a number line from 0 to 2, each whole is split into 3 equal gaps. Between which two whole numbers does 5/3 lie?
On a number line from 0 to 2, which is further from 0: 5/4 or 5/8?
Where is 6/3 on the number line?
checks.wrongIfMis: it cannot go on the number line

ladder.why: den 4 on 0 to 2, same den and line as e1, e2 and the worked example → 5/4 = one quarter past 1; smallest step beyond 1
den 3, no line given → decide before/after 1 from top vs bottom alone (4 > 3); moves the rule off the picture
den 2 inside a story: 1 km + half km → count in halves → 3/2; build the improper fraction from a real distance
den 3 again but out to 3 → 8 marks grouped in threes → past two wholes (between 2 and 3); hardest grouping

remediation.move: quarter-pieces laid end to end on a 0-to-2 line, no squeezing: 4 pieces fill 0 to 1 exactly → 1 is full → any further piece must go past 1; a fraction is a length, lengths can exceed one whole
remediation.then: running track: one lap = 1, each lap cut into 6 equal stretches; runner covers 7 stretches from the start → between which two whole laps, and the fraction

remediation.move: same top, different hop size on one 0-to-2 line cut in eighths: 5 hops of 1/8 stop before 1 (5/8); 5 hops of 1/4 = 10 eighths, past 1 (5/4 = 10/8); quarter-hop = 2 eighth-hops → bigger bottom = shorter hops

train between stations: station 0, station 1, station 2; each station-to-station stretch cut into 5 equal parts; train runs 7 parts and halts → it is at one real spot on the track → that spot is 7/5, a single number past station 1
remediation.then: line from 0 to 2, each whole cut into 5 equal parts; a marker stands 3 marks after 1 → the single fraction naming that spot
